newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas stays mixed late, Aug holds with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas stays mixed late, Aug holds with cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained narrowly mixed late Thursday in sluggish trade, with spot August still holding a slim gain on forecasts next week for warmer East Coast weather and a steady cash.

"The weather is not too exciting from a demand standpoint, but it seems to be enough to hold us up today. Apparently, no one was deterred by the (bearish) AGA number," said one Midwest trader, referring to the unexpectedly-large 96 bcf weekly stock build in last night's inventory report.

While revised forecasts are calling for warmer Midwest and East Coast weather later this week and next, he said the warmup was expected to be short-lived, with more seasonal weather forecast for later in the week.
Heat is expected to continue in Texas and the West.
At 1345 EDT, August was still up 1.2 cents at $2.11 per million British thermal units, while September was 0.3 cent higher at $2.12. Other deferreds remained narrowly mixed.

While prospects for more cooling load have helped prop up cash and nearby futures, most saw little upside without a more sustained, extreme heat wave, particularly with inventories growing more comfortable each week.

Chart traders agreed August seemed range bound, with little reason to break far in either direction. Support was seen at this week's $2.051 low, with psychological buying likely ahead of $2. Resistance was pegged first at $2.15, with major selling expected along the down trendline at $2.25.

In the cash Thursday, Gulf Coast prices mostly were down slightly in the low-teens. Midcon pipes were steady to one cent lower in the low-$2s. New York city gate gas was little changed in the high-$2.30s.
NYMEX said 18,071 contracts traded at 1315 EDT. Hub open interest on July 9 rose 1,213 contracts to 201,328.
On the KCBT, August was still up by 1.5 cents at $2.005, while deferreds were steady to one cent higher. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.3 cent to 10.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
